descriptionChirho: To be (too) high or beyond reach, describing something physically elevated beyond access or attainment (Qal stem).
To be exalted or lifted up in honor or status, typically said of God or a dignified person (Niphal passive/stative).
To be physically high or lofty, often describing fortified walls or structures that are elevated beyond easy approach (Niphal participle/perfect).
To be secure or safe by virtue of being set in an inaccessibly high position, a figurative extension of height as protection (Niphal).
To set someone securely on high, placing them in an elevated refuge out of danger's reach; hence to protect or defend (Piel intensive-causative).

labelChirho: Pual: be set securely on high
descriptionChirho: Passive of the Piel: to be placed in a high, protected position, to be safeguarded by elevation (Pual passive).
To cause to be high or exalted, to elevate someone or something in status or position (Hifil causative).
